ActorRef.description: Who an action is attributed to: `human:alice`, `agent:x`, `service:y`, `system`.

ArtifactStatus.description: Artifact status. The named vocabulary is listed in `examples`; any other name a lifecycle document declares is carried verbatim, so a rung is a line in a YAML file rather than a release of the engine.

AuditKind.description:
What sort of thing an audit record reports.

The vocabulary is logical, not physical: an implementation may collapse or expand the records it actually stores as long as every kind here stays queryable.

oneOf.description: A command passed authorisation and validation.
A command was refused; nothing changed.
An entity was archived; it remains addressable.
An entity was replaced by a newer one.
A relation between two entities was created.
A relation between two entities was removed.
The protocol engine decided whether something was permitted.
A workflow transition was evaluated and not permitted.
Evidence was recorded against a subject.
A verifier finished and reported an outcome.

anyOf.description: Who an action is attributed to: `human:alice`, `agent:x`, `service:y`, `system`.
Opaque canonical identity of an entity; never interpreted.

AuditRecord.description:
One immutable record in the audit trail.

Records are never updated in place. A correction is a new record that names the one it corrects through its [`CausationRef`], which is what makes the trail evidence rather than a mutable summary of someone's current opinion of the past.

actor.description: On whose behalf it happened, and who bears responsibility.

change.description: What changed. Absent whenever nothing did — in particular on every refusal.

command_id.description: The logical command it belongs to; retries of one intent share it.

correlation_id.description:
Which broader activity it belongs to.

Mandatory, unlike everything else that links records together: a record nobody can reach from the activity it belongs to is a record nobody will ever read.

decision.description: Why it was allowed or refused.

event_id.description: The domain event it belongs to.

evidence.description: The evidence or approvals that justified it.

execution_id.description: The protocol execution that was active.

executor.description: What actually ran, when that differs from who authorised it.

kind.description: What sort of thing it reports.

request_id.description: The transport attempt it arrived on.

task.description: The task the work belongs to.

Capability.description: A semantic capability, such as `repository.write`, `network.read:private` or `deployment.create:staging`.

CapabilityDecision.description: What a policy says about one capability.

oneOf.description: May be exercised once a matching approval has been recorded.
Explicitly forbidden; no grant can override this.
Not mentioned by the policy, and therefore not granted.

CausationRef.description:
What directly caused this record.

Causation and correlation answer different questions and are both needed. Correlation says *what belongs together* — one activity, one id, however many records. Causation says *what produced this one*, and chains: a command attempt causes a capability decision, the decision causes a denial, the denial causes an approval request. With only correlation the chain is a bag; with only causation there is no way to ask for the whole activity.

oneOf.description: An earlier decision caused this, named by the audit record that carries it.

ChangeRecord.description:
What changed, in a form the mutation can be reconstructed from.

The logical contract is only that "what changed" be recoverable: a backend may hold full revisions, patches, events or snapshots. What the record must carry is the entity, the revisions on either side of the change, and the command that caused it, so that a reader can go and fetch either side.

# Redaction

A payload may contain a secret, a customer's data or a credential, and auditability must not require storing any of it. So the payload is droppable — but nothing else is. Attribution (`actor`, `executor`), causality (`correlation_id`, `causation`), the entity and its revisions and the reason for redaction all survive, because they are what the audit is *for*: after redaction the trail can still say who did what to which entity and why the content is absent. A redaction that took the actor with it would answer nothing, and would make redaction a way to hide rather than a way to protect.

after.description: The revision after the change; absent when the entity no longer has a current revision.

before.description: The revision before the change; absent when the entity did not exist yet.

command.description:
The name of the command that caused it, such as `design.approve`.

Held as a name rather than a typed command so that the audit model does not depend on the command vocabulary, which changes far more often than the audit trail's readers do.

payload.description: The command payload, when it may be stored.

redacted.description:
Whether the payload was withheld.

Distinct from `payload: None`, which means there was nothing to record. This says there *was* a payload and it is deliberately not here.

redaction_reason.description: Why the payload was withheld, such as `contains-credential`.

Command.description:
A state-changing operation.

The generic variants are the ones every entity type supports; the domain variants exist because their transitions carry conditions a field assignment cannot express. See the module documentation for why both kinds are needed.

data.description: The body, in whatever shape the entity type declares.

entity_type.description: What kind of entity it is, which decides its schema, lifecycle and permitted relations.

locator.description: The address it is to be known by.

oneOf.description: Change an entity's ordinary mutable fields.

changes.description: The fields to set, keyed by field name.

source.description: Where the edge starts; relation kinds are read source-first, `source specifies target`.

oneOf.description: Take an entity out of active use.

reason.description: Why, recorded in the audit trail.

oneOf.description: Replace an entity with a successor.

reason.description: Why, recorded in the audit trail.

oneOf.description: Ask for a review of a design revision.

design.description: The exact revision to be reviewed; a review of "the design" would not survive the next edit.

review.description: The review that supports the approval.

supersedes.description:
The decision this one reverses, when it reverses one.

Carried on the acceptance rather than issued as a separate [`SupersedeEntity`] because the two facts are one decision: an ADR that supersedes another does so *by being accepted*, and splitting it in two leaves a window in which both are current.

oneOf.description: Move an artifact along its declared status ladder.

decided_on.description:
The account of what the decision rested on, as the caller recorded it.

Carried as data rather than as a type, because the shape belongs to whatever recorded it — a store's journal, an audit trail — and the command vocabulary is not the place to fix one. What matters here is that it **travels with the move**: the difference between a status somebody asserted the evidence for and one a record established is the difference `story:completion-needs-evidence` exists over, and a move that arrived without its account would lose it silently.

expected_revision.description: The revision the caller expected, when it stated one.

to.description: The status it moved to, as the kind's ladder spells it.

oneOf.description: Record an observation about an artifact.

kind.description: What kind of observation it is.

outcome.description: What became of that review: `no-op`, `fixed` or `escalated`.

reference.description: What it points at — a run, a digest, a suite's own words.

review.description:
The review this observation answers, for a [`ReviewOutcome`](crate::evidence::EvidenceKind::ReviewOutcome) record.

# Why the generic command carries it

A review is immutable once recorded, so what became of it cannot be an edit to it and has to be a later record referencing it (`epic:review-facts`). That record is evidence about the *reviewed* artifact — which review it answers is therefore not derivable from the target, and a record that did not name it would say only that *some* review was acted on. Both keys are optional and every other kind leaves them unset; the edge refuses the combinations that do not make sense, because the check needs the store (does that review review this artifact) and this type has none.

source.description: Where it came from, as the recorder is willing to say.

target.description: Which artifact the observation is about.

command_type.description: Its versioned wire name, such as `aep.design.approve/v1`.

revision_guarded.description: Whether it asserts a revision, and so cannot silently overwrite.

summary.description: What it does, in one line.

oneOf.description: Recognised as a replay of a command already applied; the original result is returned.
Accepted, and nothing changed — the state already matched.

CommandRequestV1.description: A version-1 command request before the server adds trusted context.

causation.description: The direct cause, explicitly null when absent.

execution_id.description: The protocol execution, explicitly null when absent.

expected_revision.description: The asserted revision, explicitly null when absent.

anyOf.description: Opaque canonical identity of an entity; never interpreted.

target.description: The command target, explicitly null when absent.

task.description: The governed task, explicitly null when absent.

CommandRequestV1.title: CommandRequestV1

CommandResultV1.description: A command result whose empty collections are still written on the wire.

audit.description: Audit records emitted by the command.

consistency.description: Token a subsequent read may demand.

outcome.description: Whether this was the first application, a replay or a no-op.

DecisionRecord.description:
Why the protocol allowed or refused something, in a form a person can read back.

This is the shape a refusal takes in the trail. "Denied" on its own is unusable six months later: the reader needs the operation that was attempted, the rule that refused it, what was missing, and the state the execution was in — because the same operation is often allowed one state later, and the record has to make that visible.

capability.description: The capability it needed, when the decision was a capability decision.

decision.description: What the resolved policy said about that capability.

missing.description:
What was missing, such as `approval:production-change`.

This is the "what would have stopped it" half of the record: it tells a reader what to obtain in order to make the same attempt succeed.

rule.description: The named rule that decided it, such as `production-write-requires-approval`.

source.description:
Which document decided it.

This also carries "which principle refused this": [`PolicySource::Principle`] names it, so the record does not need a separate principle field.

state.description: The workflow state the execution was in when the decision was made.

EntityId.description: Opaque canonical identity of an entity; never interpreted.

EntityLocator.description: Logical address of an entity: `ep://<organisation>/<space>/<kind>/<key>`. Not a storage URL.

EntityMetadata.description: What every entity carries, whatever its type.

provenance.description: Who made it and who changed it.

revision.description: How many times it has changed.

EntityProvenance.description: How an entity came to exist and change.

created_executor.description: What ran, when that differs from who authorised it.

source_revision.description: The source revision it describes, for generated entities.

updated_executor.description: What ran for the last change.

anyOf.description: Opaque canonical identity of an entity; never interpreted.
The meaning of an edge in the artifact graph.

oneOf.description: Shaped by, without being derived from.
Breaks a larger artifact into smaller work.
States the required behaviour of something.
Records a decision taken within something.
Produces the outcome something asked for.
Moves an objective the collection has set — a `vision` artifact — and says which.

Entity_for_Node.description: An entity: metadata plus its typed body.

EvidenceKind.description: A kind of evidence. The canonical names come first; the rest are older spellings still accepted.

HistoryQueryV2.description: A strict version-2 bounded history request.

after.description: Continuation, explicitly null for the first page.

limit.description: Maximum records, explicitly null for the server default.

HistoryQueryV2.title: HistoryQueryV2

requires.description:
Which rungs cost evidence, and of which kind, how many — `to -> [(kind, at_least)]`.

Empty for a ladder that only says which moves are legal. A harness that reads this knows before it asks that `implemented` needs a `test_result`, which is the whole of gap-register `:39` read from the far side.

Node.description: Any JSON/YAML value: null, boolean, number, string, array or object.

PageV1_for_AuditRecord.description: A page whose nullable continuation member is always present.

next.description: Continuation cursor, explicitly null on the last page.

next.description: Continuation cursor, explicitly null on the last page.

PolicySource.description: Which document contributed a policy entry, so a denial can be explained.

ProblemV1.description: A stable failure and safe structured details selected by its code.

details.description: Code-specific safe details, validated when mapped to the semantic error.

message.description: Diagnostic text, not a machine contract.

retryable.description: Whether retrying unchanged intent may succeed later.

QueryConsistency.description: How fresh a read has to be.

oneOf.description: Whatever the backend has now. The default, and the cheap one.
A view no older than the successful command that produced this token.

Relation.description: A relation in the entity graph.

id.description: Its identity, so it can be removed by name.

RelationDescriptor.description: A relation this type may have.
